newsitem.title: UK: UK may allow more slot machines in casinos.
newsitem.headline: UK may allow more slot machines in casinos.

text.p: The British government on Tuesday published fresh proposals for the deregulation of the casino industry, suggesting clubs should be allowed to have up to three slot machines per gaming table.
The move would allow London's largest casinos to have up to 100 "one-arm bandits", marking a huge change in the nature of British gaming houses which have traditionally relied mainly on table games.
The proposal contrasts with a consultation paper published earlier this year which suggested that casinos be allowed two slot machines per gaming table.

The government suggested in its new consultation document that casinos should be allowed in seven "conference towns" where they are at present banned. The towns are Bath, Eastbourne, Exeter, Harrogate, Norwich, Telford and York.
It also said East London, including the Docklands area, should be considered. At present casinos are only allowed in central London.
The earlier consultation document suggested 13 other towns which should be opened to the industry, but councils in two of these, Peterborough and Croydon, have said they do not want gaming houses.
Among other proposals announced by Home Office minister Timothy Kirkhope were some which had been trailed in the previous document.

Members of a casino would have immediate access to gaming facilities in other casinos in the same group instead of having to make a separate membership application, and postal applications for membership would be allowed.
And casinos would be allowed to advertise their existence in non-national publications including newspapers and magazines.
The government has asked for responses to its proposals by the end of January. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
